title: Is it a fact or an opinion?
examples: What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?
How can I tell if something is a fact?

explain.say: Your friend says, Mangoes are the best fruit in the world! Is that true? Well, for your friend maybe, but not for everyone. Look at the board. Statements get sorted into two boxes. The first box is facts.

draw.text: Is it a fact or an opinion?

explain.say: A fact is something that can be checked and proved true. The Nile is a very long river. Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level. Lima is in Peru. You could look them up. Can you tell me one fact about where you live?

Now look at the other box: opinions. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels. Maths is fun. Rain is boring. Some people agree, some don't, and nobody can prove it. What is your opinion about football?

Here is a detective tip: look for opinion words. Best, worst, beautiful, boring, I think, I believe. See them in the opinion box? Facts often have numbers, dates or names you can check. Which word gives away Mangoes are best?
Fantastic! Adverts and news often mix facts and opinions, so spotting them makes you a smart reader. Look at the whole board. Challenge: turn the opinion Rain is boring into a fact about rain.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?
faq.a: A fact can be checked and proved, like Lima is in Peru. An opinion is what someone thinks or feels, like Lima is the best city, and cannot be proved.

faq.q: How can I tell if something is a fact?
faq.a: Ask: could I check this in a reliable book, a measurement or a record? If yes, it is a fact, even if it turns out to be wrong.
Words like best, worst, beautiful, boring, should, I think and I believe usually show an opinion.
An opinion cannot be proved right or wrong, but a good opinion is backed up with reasons and facts.

faq.q: Why do adverts mix facts and opinions?
faq.a: Adverts want you to buy something, so they mix real facts with opinions like the tastiest snack ever. Spotting the opinions helps you decide for yourself.

facts: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level; on high mountains it boils at a lower temperature.
The Nile, at about 6,650 kilometres, is usually listed as the longest river in the world.
